newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: San Miguel hit by heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: San Miguel hit by heavy selling.

text.p: Food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp was hit by heavy selling in early trade as investors took a slightly bearish view of the group's recent sale of its majority stake in a Coca-Cola bottling unit, analysts said.
San Miguel A shares lost one peso to 54 pesos, while its B shares, which are open to foreign investors, shed 1.50 pesos to 79.50 pesos after falling to 75.50 pesos earlier.
"San Miguel shares are very volatile. A lot of investors see the deal as disadvantageous to San Miguel," Carla Garcia, an analyst of Anping & Associates, said.
San Miguel's Coca-Cola operation is one of its most profitable subsidiaries.
"San Miguel is trading short-term gains for some potential gains which may or may not happen in the future," another analyst said.
San Miguel last week announced its plan to merge its softdrink unit with Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd in exchange for a 25 percent equity stake in Coca-Cola Amatil.
